## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Goṇapetavatthu* ("The Ox", Pv 8) is a verse narrative in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. Centering on the theme of consoling those overwhelmed by bereavement, the text addresses how one can help individuals stricken with grief. In modern scholarship, B. C. Law mentions the story of the *Gonapeta* among various ghost accounts explored in his monograph *The Buddhist Conception of Spirits* [Law 1926].

 Computational analysis by DharmaNexus confirms substantial Pali-internal text reuse between the verses of Pv 8 (§4–8) and these shared grief narratives, showing close alignment with the *Sujātajātaka*, *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka*, *Kaṇhapetavatthu*, *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka*, *Migapotakajātaka*, and *Somadattajātaka*, as well as their commentaries in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels are recorded in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
